query: Why do expense decline rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing expenses (hardware/travel/software) gives a strong new axis to explain why decline rates differ across departments, since spend composition varies by department. Values are well-grounded in short_description and ci text.

per_column.name: device_form_factor
per_column.rationale: A finer-grained breakdown of asset type; adds a useful axis for spend composition analysis, though partly redundant with asset_category_type. Values are soundly read from ci/short_description, with reasonable NULLs.

per_column.name: entry_origin
per_column.rationale: Whether an entry is manual vs auto-generated could plausibly relate to review/decline behavior, giving some analytical leverage. However groundedness is weak: the source samples show no clear textual signal distinguishing manual from auto entries, so the labeling basis is unclear and possibly inferred from source_id presence.

per_column.name: vendor_brand
per_column.rationale: Vendor is a legitimate axis for comparing decline rates and cost patterns across departments. Values are extracted well from text (Dell, HP), with 'Other' a reasonable fallback.

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean that is largely redundant with asset_category_type's 'travel' value; adds little independent leverage. Well grounded in text.

per_column.name: ci_identifier_quality
per_column.rationale: Identifier quality is a data-hygiene meta-attribute with a plausible but weak link to why expenses are declined. The sample 'ISP Services' labeled 'standard_model_name' is questionable, suggesting inconsistent grounding.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: This is a trivial presence flag derived directly from the existing source_id column, offering little new analytical leverage for the decline-rate query. Values are trivially derivable and grounded.

per_column.name: recurring_submitter
per_column.rationale: Recurring submitters could correlate with decline patterns, offering a genuine behavioral axis. But this requires aggregation over the 'user' column and cannot be verified from single-row text samples; the basis is not clearly grounded in the shown evidence.

judge.rationale: The strongest columns (asset_category_type, vendor_brand, device_form_factor) provide genuine new axes on expense composition that plausibly explain departmental differences in decline rates and are soundly grounded in the text. Several columns are weaker: is_travel_related and has_source_id are near-redundant/trivial flags, while entry_origin, ci_identifier_quality, and recurring_submitter have unclear textual grounding in the shown evidence. Overall the set offers moderate analytical value with mostly acceptable but uneven groundedness.
